# Europeanisation and the economy {#europeanisation-and-the-economy .unnumbered .unlisted}

::: {.home-lead}
Applied Replication for Data Skills (AR4DS) is a course that introduces technical skills for modern empirical data analysis through an applied 'replication' exercise. This site presents one of its case studies, built around a single published claim, its reanalysis by five independent analysts and its replication with new data.
:::

::: {.home-cta}
[Formats](#formats) [Read the background](background.qmd)
:::

## The course {#the-course .unnumbered}

::: {.home-intro}
The main aim of the course is to introduce technical skills for modern empirical data analysis: finding the data and code of a study in an online repository, working with code so that another person (or your future self) can reproduce your steps, fixing your analytical choices in a preregistration before you run the analysis, and writing a live report that combines code and text.
:::

The claim at the centre of the exercise comes from the work of SCORE, a programme that put claims from published social and behavioural research through reproduction, robustness checks and replication. The exercise follows the design of its robustness study [Multi100\; @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness] on a smaller scale, with many analysts testing the same claim, each stating their analytical choices, and results reported in a form that allows them to be compared. The AR4DS site describes [the programme](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/score.html), and its page on [the robustness article](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/robustness-article.html) explains how the results of the analysts were placed on one scale and compared.

::::

:::: {.home-rs .home-reveal}

::: {.home-r}
### Reproduction {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Participants choose one of the three reanalyses fitted on aggregate data and repeat it step by step, recovering the recorded test statistic to the third decimal and establishing why the analysts arrived at such different estimates.
:::

::: {.home-r}
### Robustness {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Participants then work through the analytical decisions that lie between the data and a result, trying alternative specifications one change at a time, locating each result on a specification curve of `r e_spec` defensible analyses and – in the day and independent formats – declaring one specification in a short preregistration before it is run.
:::

::: {.home-r}
### Replication {.unnumbered .unlisted}

The course then sets the claim against its replication on fourteen later Eurobarometer waves, judged not successful by SCORE, and considers what a failed replication can and cannot establish about the original result.
:::

## The case study {#the-case .unnumbered}

::: {.home-intro}
The case study is built around an article published in the *European Sociological Review* in 2016, which drew on Eurobarometer surveys conducted between 2004 and 2013 to examine whether the economic crisis had changed the meanings that citizens attach to the European Union, or what its author calls 'EU framing'. One sentence of its abstract, in the form given to the analysts of the robustness study, became the claim tested in the course:
:::

> "... poor economic performances ... decrease positive dimensions of EU framing" [@Teney2016DoesEUEconomic, p. 619]

::: {.home-cta}
[Read the background](background.qmd)
:::

::::

:::: {.home-rs .home-reveal}

::: {.home-r}
### Methods {.unnumbered .unlisted}

The aggregation of repeated cross-sections into a panel, fixed and random effects and the within–between model, inference with few clusters, and a multiverse of `r e_spec` specifications.
:::

::: {.home-r}
### Data {.unnumbered .unlisted}

A panel of `r e_cells` country-years built from the Eurobarometer surveys and shipped with the workspace. The respondent files behind it come from the GESIS archive, under a free account and terms that do not allow them to be passed on. Extending the analysis to later waves, as the SCORE replicability study did with fourteen waves fielded between 2013 and 2019, needs the respondent files of those waves from GESIS, under the same terms, and the unemployment and growth series of the World Bank for the same years.
:::

## Formats {.unnumbered .home-reveal}

::: {.home-intro .home-reveal}
The facilitator of a course chooses its format, and the link that you receive for a course leads to it, as does the card of each format below.
:::

:::: {.home-grid}

::: {.home-track .home-reveal}
### [Short](tracks/short/index.qmd) {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[Two halves, with R inside the slides]{.home-meta}

Three hours on the claim and its five reanalyses, with nothing to install and nothing preregistered: the estimand statement, the reproduction of one recorded result, the specification menu with your own tries on the class chart, the curve of 864 and how to read it, and the replication with new data.
:::

::: {.home-track .home-reveal}
### [Day](tracks/day/index.qmd) {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[Four parts, in the workspace]{.home-meta}

The claim and the credibility of social science, with the record of the paper in SCORE, the estimand and the causal graph, the reproduction of one of the reanalyses that worked on country-years, chosen by each participant, and the robustness exercise: the specification menu, the class chart and its submissions, the curve of the claim, and one analysis declared before it runs.
:::

::: {.home-track .home-reveal}
### [Independent](tracks/independent/index.qmd) {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[At your own pace, in R]{.home-meta}

The case study for a reader who works alone, in R on your own machine, with the modules of the [companion](companion/index.qmd) between the tasks of the exercise and a project of your own at the end.
:::

## The exercise {.unnumbered .home-reveal}

::: {.home-intro .home-reveal}
The day and independent formats work through the same five tasks in the workspace, and the short format takes three of them in its deck. The decisions that the tasks ask for fall into three groups: those about the question that the analysis answers, those about how the variables are measured, and those about the model, how it is fitted and how its uncertainty is judged.
:::

:::: {.home-reveal}

<details>
<summary><span class="home-n">Task 1</span>The setup check</summary>

Check that your tools work before the rest of the work depends on them: the check script of the workspace, or the setup cell of the deck in the short format.

</details>

<details>
<summary><span class="home-n">Task 2</span>The panel, the estimand and the graph</summary>

Meet the country-year panel, write the estimand statement behind the claim, and finish the causal graph that goes with it. The graph shows what the fixed effects of a country-year panel do and do not absorb.

</details>

<details>
<summary><span class="home-n">Task 3</span>The reproduction</summary>

Choose one of the three analysts who fitted their models on means of countries or of cells, and reproduce the value recorded in the robustness study for that analyst, from the data behind it. The other two analysts worked on respondents, whose files only a GESIS account can give.

</details>

<details>
<summary><span class="home-n">Task 4</span>The menu</summary>

Work through the decisions that lie between the data and a result, try alternatives one change at a time, and send one exploration to the class chart. The [decision map](menu.qmd#map) lays every decision out.

</details>

<details>
<summary><span class="home-n">Task 5</span>Preregistration</summary>

Declare one specification in a short preregistration, run it, report it, and find where it sits among the `r e_spec` specifications of the [curve of the claim](curve.qmd).

</details>

::::

The exercise page of each format sets out its tasks in full, with the tool in which each is done: the [short](tracks/short/exercise.qmd), [day](tracks/day/exercise.qmd) and [independent](tracks/independent/exercise.qmd) formats.

## Getting started {.unnumbered .home-reveal}

::: {.home-intro .home-reveal}
The short format needs nothing installed, because its deck runs R inside the browser. The day and independent formats work in the workspace, with R, Quarto and an IDE installed beforehand, and in the day format the deck shows each step with its output. The browser lab holds every task as the fallback.
:::

:::: {.home-steps .home-reveal}

::: {.home-step}
### R and an IDE {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Install R, Quarto and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), following the steps for your operating system; the [setup help](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that others have met. [Install and check](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html)
:::

::: {.home-step}
### The workspace {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Download the workspace of the case study as a zip file, open it in your IDE and run the check script. The report of the workspace, with the output of every chunk, is published on [a site of its own](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-eu-workspace/). [Download the workspace](tracks/day/before.qmd#the-workspace)
:::

::: {.home-step}
### The browser lab {.unnumbered .unlisted}

The lab holds every task of the exercise in the browser, with nothing to install, and is the fallback when a machine or an installation fails on the day. [Open the browser lab](lab.qmd)
:::

## Chris Moreh {.unnumbered}

::: {.home-role}
Lecturer in Sociology, Newcastle University
:::

<!-- The biography is quoted from chrismoreh.com (source: D:/GitHub/chrismoreh-source/index.qmd), as CM asked on 2026-10-25. -->

A social scientist interested in the political sociology of migration, mobility, ethnicity and nationalism.

Hailing from Transylvania, trained in anthropology and sociology at [Eötvös Loránd University of Budapest](https://tatk.elte.hu/en/) and [Central European University](https://sociology.ceu.edu/), and with a PhD from [Northumbria University](https://www.northumbria.ac.uk/), I currently work as a Lecturer (Assistant Professor) in Sociology at [Newcastle University (UK)](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/gps/staff/profile/chrismoreh.html).

I approach social research as a comparative, interdisciplinary and multimethodological endeavour. My work has combined ethnographic observation, document analysis, survey methods and statistical modelling.

I'm enthusiastic about transparency and reproducibility in the social sciences, and my [pedagogical approach](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/mediav8/library/file-downloads/research-services/open-research/moreh.pdf) seeks to develop skills that facilitate open and credible research practices.

[chrismoreh.com](https://chrismoreh.com)
